newsitem.title: USA: KCBT March wheat ends up on weather, others drop.
newsitem.headline: KCBT March wheat ends up on weather, others drop.

text.p: KCBT nearby March hard red winter wheat closed higher on slow movement of wheat due to harsh winter weather, traders said.
"It's on the transportation slowdown and the cash basis is firm but there wasn't a lot going on," a trader said of closing gains in the March.
Wheat closed 2-3/4 cents per bushel higher to two lower, with March up 2-3/4 at $4.18-1/2.
Traders said the nearby cash basis market was firm, reflecting the slowdown in wheat movment due to snow and bitter cold winter weather.
The March/May widened to close at 36 cents per bushel, premium the March. The March/May closed Tuesday at 32-3/4 cents, premium March.
Cargill Inc was an early buyer and set the tone for the day, traders said.
"They (Cargill) started buying at 14-1/2, again at 15 and at 16," one trader said.
News Algeria bought another 50,000 tonnes of wheat from France rather than the U.S. curbed gains in nearbys.
New crop July sagged on diminished concern about cold weather damage to the U.S. winter wheat crop.
Much of the U.S. winter wheat crop is now safely insulated by a snow cover.
At 1005 CST, KCBT wheat was 3/4 cent per bushel higher to 1-1/2 lower, with March up 3/4 at $4.16-1/2.
